A vessel a dog drinks from is washed seven times, a man entered Paradise for watering a thirsty dog, and no water was sprinkled where dogs urinated in the mosques.
A muhrim may kill five harmful animals, crow, kite, mouse, scorpion and rabid dog, even in the sanctuary; a snake at Mina was ordered killed, and the salamander called bad.
Keeping a dog not guarding farms or cattle, or hunting, costs a Qirat of reward daily; a cow says it was made for ploughing, and a wolf speaks.
A man who watered a thirsty dog was forgiven, as serving any living being earns reward, and a woman entered Hell for locking up a cat until it starved.
One of the rights of a she-camel is that it be milked at a place of water.
A man who climbed down a well to water a thirsty dog was forgiven, as serving any living being earns reward.
On one of his journeys the Prophet sent a messenger ordering that no string or other necklace be left round camels' necks.
An ant bit a prophet, who had its colony burnt, and Allah rebuked him for burning a whole nation that glorifies Allah because one ant bit him.
The Prophet ordered snakes killed, especially those with two white lines or a short tail, which blind and cause abortion, but later forbade killing snakes living in houses.
Salamanders and snakes with two white lines or short tails are ordered killed, house snakes spared; five harmful animals, rats included, may be killed in the Sanctuary or Ihram.
A woman entered Hell for starving a cat, a prostitute was forgiven for watering a dog, a prophet was rebuked for burning ants, and needless dogs cost a Qirat daily.
An Israelite prostitute took off her shoe to water a dog dying of thirst, and Allah forgave her for it.
A woman entered the Fire because of a cat she imprisoned until it died, neither feeding it nor setting it free to find food.
Whoever keeps a dog not for hunting or guarding livestock loses two qirats of reward each day.
Anas and Ibn Umar, seeing boys shoot at a tied hen, said the Prophet forbade killing tied animals, cursed mutilating a live one, and forbade An-Nuhba.
Ibn Umar disliked branding animals on the face, as the Prophet forbade striking the face, while Anas saw the Prophet branding a sheep, on its ear he thought.
A thirsty man who went down a well again to water a panting dog was forgiven by Allah, and there is reward for serving any living being.
